steps.text: Litmus is the classic acid–base indicator. Pick a solution, dip the paper, and watch the colour change.
First pick an acid — tap the lemon (lemon juice is an acid).
Now tap “Dip Papers” to dip the litmus paper into it.
Look: blue litmus turns RED. A change to red means the solution is an ACID.
Now pick a base — tap the soap.
Tap “Dip Papers” again to test the soap.
This time red litmus turns BLUE — that means the solution is a BASE. (Try water too — neither colour changes, so it's neutral.)

coach.mission: Use litmus to sort acids from bases.
whenStuck: Pick a solution first, then tap “Dip Papers”.
Nothing changes until you dip — pick a solution, then dip the paper.
whenWrong: Blue litmus turns red in an ACID; red litmus turns blue in a BASE — check which colour changed.
No change? The solution may be neutral, like water.
whenCorrect: Correct — you read the litmus right!
Acid turns litmus red, base turns it blue. Nicely done.
coach.done: You can tell acids, bases and neutrals with litmus now. Try the other solutions, or move on.
